card: Decouples BlockManager ownership from ChainstateManager by instantiating it in NodeContext and the kernel and passing it to ChainstateManager by reference. Currently, block storage cannot exist independently of chainstate management, preventing kernel use cases such as working with pruned block directories. The author cites issue #35627 as the motivation for decoupling these components. This PR depends on base PR #36738.
evidence: PR description cites issue #35627 ('kernel: can't work with pruned blocksdir'), noting that 'moving that ownership out of ChainstateManager... came up as worthwhile doing.'
problem: ChainstateManager currently instantiates and owns BlockManager, preventing block storage from existing independently of chainstate validation. This architecture impedes kernel library decoupling, including work needed to address issue #35627 where the kernel cannot work with a pruned block directory.

risk.why: Altering the lifecycle, initialization order, and flush/prune coordination between BlockManager and ChainstateManager could cause shutdown crashes, use-after-free, or missed block index flushes.

scope_notes: The PR is stacked on #36738, so several commits (such as block storage writes and prune flush error handling) belong to the base PR. The diff was omitted from the prompt.
summary: Decouples BlockManager lifecycle from ChainstateManager by instantiating BlockManager in NodeContext and the kernel, then passing it to ChainstateManager by reference. Replaces BlockManager friend class declarations with explicit methods (RequestPrune and MarkBlockIndexDirty) and moves ImportBlocks to node/chainstate. Also eliminates the redundant ChainstateLoadOptions::prune setting.
uncertainties: Diff was omitted, so commit boundaries and changes specific to this PR versus base PR #36738 cannot be fully verified.
